Article.ArticleTitle: Blood-borne Interleukin-1β Acts upon the Subfornical Organ to Upregulate the Sympathoexcitatory Milieu of the Hypothalamic Paraventricular Nucleus.

Abstract.AbstractText: We previously reported that microinjection of the pro-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) into the subfornical organ (SFO) elicits a pressor response accompanied by increases in inflammation and renin-angiotensin system (RAS) activity in the SFO and in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN). The present study sought to determine whether blood-borne IL-1β induces similar neurochemical changes in the SFO and PVN, and, if so, whether increased inflammation and RAS activity at the SFO level orchestrate the sympathoexcitatory response to circulating IL-1β. In urethane-anesthetized male Sprague-Dawley rats, intravenous injection of IL-1β (500 ng) increased blood pressure, heart rate and renal sympathetic nerve activity, and increased mRNA for angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE), angiotensin II type-1a receptor (AT1aR), cyclooxygenase (COX)-2, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and IL-1β, as well as the TNF-α p55 receptor (TNFR1) and the IL-1 receptor (IL-1R) in SFO and PVN. Pretreatment with SFO microinjections of the AT1R blocker losartan (1 µg), the ACE inhibitor captopril (1 µg) or the COX-2 inhibitor NS398 (2 µg) attenuated the expression of these excitatory mediators in SFO and downstream in PVN and the IL-1β-induced pressor responses. An SFO lesion minimized the IL-1β-induced expression of inflammatory and RAS components as well as c-Fos, an indicator of neuronal excitation, in PVN. These studies demonstrate that circulating IL-1β, which increases in cardiovascular disorders such as hypertension and heart failure, acts upon the SFO to increase inflammation and RAS activity in SFO and PVN, and that intervening in these neurochemical processes in the SFO can significantly reduce the sympathetic response.
